[0] everyday_reading (E): Everyday meaning: to 'compile' is to gather or put together (compile a list), and 'running' a program sounds like it starts on its own. Java rule: compiling with javac only translates Name.java into bytecode in Name.class; nothing executes until java Name is typed.
[1] misconception (M) -> CompileRunsProgram: wrong rule: Compiling also executes the program. Right rule: javac only translates Name.java into Name.class; the program runs only with java Name, and run-time errors can appear then.
[2] misconception (M) -> CompilesMeansWorks: wrong rule: Code that compiles is code that works. Right rule: Code that compiles can still have run-time errors and logic errors.
[3] inconsistent_trace (T) -> CompileRunsProgram: Applies the compile rule (LT) unevenly: expects output after javac on one try but not another, or runs java Name after a failed compile as if the old Name.class reflected the new edits. (here mixing in: "compiling also executes the program")

[0] names_the_element (N): Compiling is translating the whole Java source file into a lower-level form (Java bytecode) before execution; javac is the Java compiler.
[1] states_the_rule (S): javac Name.java takes the file Name.java as input and, if there are no compile-time errors, produces Name.class (the bytecode version) with the same name.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): The compiler first reads (parses) the entire file, then translates it; it does all this before the program starts running, and only if no errors were found does it write Name.class.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Result of javac Name.java: either a new file Name.class and no terminal output, or a list of error messages (file:line: message, then 'N errors') and no Name.class.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): One compile changes only the file system: it creates or overwrites Name.class; it changes no program variable and prints no program output.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): java Name loads the Name.class made by javac, so a successful compile must come before running, and edits take effect only after recompiling.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): A compile-time error stops the translation, so no Name.class is produced and there is nothing new to run.
[2] relation_to_neighbour (R): javac takes the program text Name.java as input; its file name must match the public class name.
[3] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Purpose: check the program against the language rules and turn it into a form the JVM can execute, once, so it can then be run repeatedly with different inputs.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> CompileRunsProgram: Recompiling the same unchanged source gives the same Name.class; any edit to the source is invisible to java Name until recompiled; adding or deleting comments or whitespace changes nothing the program does.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Compile after every change before running, and compile often while making small changes, so each error is found close to its cause; compiling cannot find run-time or logic errors.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Source must obey Java's syntax and type rules. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: any syntax error (missing ; or brace, misspelled keyword) or type error in Name.java
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: javac needs the .java file name. Kind: launch error. Trigger class: typing javac Name (no .java) or the wrong file name / directory
